newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share traders run for cover as IBIS tumbles.
newsitem.headline: German share traders run for cover as IBIS tumbles.

text.p: German shares took a serious roasting in afternoon trade on the IBIS DAX index on Friday, as sliding futures and a dramatic drop on Wall Street pushed the DAX below the 4,100-point level in a flash-fire correction.
By 1351 GMT the IBIS DAX index was down 127.53 points, or 3.04 percent, at 4068.34 points, while the September DAX future contract was down 116 points at 4,082 points.
"A lot of people are running for cover out there at the moment. This is very quickly done -- it's a bit of a fast correction -- but just look at how the future has fallen," one Frankfurt trader.
"Volumes are thin out there, but the momentum is strong," he said.

The Dow Jones Industrial index tumbled over 100 points in early trade amid fears for the weakening dollar, the inability of bonds to rally despite benign inflation data and concerns over earnings at Gillette.
A number of major investment banks cut their earnings per share (EPS) outlook for Gillette on worries about the performance of its Braun unit.
The Dow Jones Industrial was down 0.99 percent at 7,864.68 points after a half-hour of trade.
The dollar lost a lot of ground over the day and stood at around 1.82 marks in afternoon trade.
Losses were across the board on the IBIS DAX. Chemicals, under pressure of late after releasing first-half figures which were just in line with forecasts, were among loss-leaders.

BASF AG was down 1.90 marks at 65.90 mark, Hoechst AG was down 2.30 marks at 73.40 marks, while the other chemical stock in the triumvirate, Bayer AG, expected to report on Tuesday, was down 3.01 marks at 70.14 marks.
Carmakers were also under pressure. Volkswagen AG was down 58.20 marks, or 4.43 percent, at 1,255 marks.
